blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Possible, not Yes. The 2026-10-19 supply census/live API reports Ethereum 64.7252%, Sonic 16.1395%, Fraxtal 10.0079%, Katana 9.1270% and Ronin 0.0003%. A direct raw-supply cross-check of authored Ethereum, Sonic, Fraxtal and Katana deployments at the pins below totals 1310650.787209937 dUSD units; Fraxtal 131169.293222 / that total =10.00795%, confirming materiality (the tiny Ronin remainder does not affect it). Ethereum block 26224761 (2026-10-19T06:14:23Z) confirms token 0x07fff99e1664d9b116fbc158c0e99785f81ca236 uses implementation 0x6f83cbdf37863eaf43d11b3af1d024c336814d1b and hasRole(PAUSER_ROLE,0x04401537CA997a43EBCFEc8194c7e88c7ee79804)=true, paused()=false; the Safe threshold is 3. Sonic block 81283161 (2026-10-19T06:16:06Z) confirms implementation 0xa140c97eff565d50cfd320fe66d27c466cc0d327 and active PAUSER_ROLE at 0xE83c188a7BE46B90715C757A06cF917175f30262, paused()=false. Their exact verified token sources implement global transfer pause; standard burnFrom spends allowance, not privileged seizure. Fraxtal block 42789902 (2026-10-19T06:15:15Z) confirms implementation 0xaf2d757bfbded5f84f71d28223acda06352fddb6 and active PAUSER_ROLE at 0xABfBcf92986B4Ba43FaAecf545F0b2Cc45067af9, paused()=false. Unlike Ethereum/Sonic, that exact implementation has COMPLIANCE_ROLE-gated freeze/unfreeze/seize. No COMPLIANCE_ROLE grant exists in complete proxy RoleGranted history through the pin (15 grants for other roles), so no active direct freeze role is established; DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE holder 0x0bafada2a5824864720873ee40cd960b36445212 can grant it, which is a mutable holder-facing Possible path. Katana at block 45647923 also has a live global pauser but is below 10%. No declared parent applies. Upstream freezable reserves remain secondary exposure; the aggregate reserve row does not establish a measured >50%, and no reserve-majority claim is used. Global pause and role-admin activation are direct Possible under the public exposure contract, irrespective of governance delay.

oracleRisk.summary: dUSD's own price is hard-coded at $1 for mint, redeem, and dLEND lending/borrowing to resist manipulation, but the protocol values its yield-bearing reserve stablecoins (e.g. sfrxUSD, sUSDS) and dLEND collateral through external feeds, API3 and Redstone, with Chainlink and issuer feeds, and those feeds drive reserve NAV and mint/redeem ratios. No documented single-primary-with-failover oracle architecture per asset.

branchApplicability.reviewer: OpenAI Codex external-a oracle applicability review
branchApplicability.rationale: dUSD is not a borrower-owned CDP position and is disabled as dLEND collateral, so it has no dUSD-specific liquidation branches. Its reserve vault nevertheless reads asset prices to value supported collateral and determine reserve-asset mint/redemption amounts, making the shared reserve valuation path a price-sensitive top-level authority.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: dTRINITY is chain-isolated by design: dUSD on Ethereum, Sonic, Katana, and Fraxtal are separately-issued non-fungible deployments, each administered by dTRINITY's own governance (1-day timelocked 3-of-5 Safes on Ethereum/Katana/Fraxtal; direct 3-of-5 Safe on Sonic). No third-party bridge controls dUSD minting anywhere.

nativeInventoryReview.reviewer: Pharos engineering W4-D5 primary native census review
nativeInventoryReview.rationale: The issuer explicitly describes technically and economically distinct chain-isolated liabilities, not cross-chain fungible dUSD representations. Its cross-chain examples redeem/swap into a different intermediary asset before bridging. The exact Ethereum, Fraxtal, Katana and historically reviewed Sonic native identities and local role observations are retained below; Sonic is retained even though the current-network prose no longer lists it. Any captured unmatched chain row remains supply-bearing and unclassified, and is allowed only while every such share independently meets the policy dust limit.
